title: Require Domain Operation Strategy Import Boundaries
forbids: domain operation strategy implementation aggregates or leaves outside their singular default-export and role-specific positive dependency surfaces
why: A semantic module is a router, while each operation strategy is one swappable definition-and-implementation leaf under one local operation. The leaf config owns the semantic id and authored configuration schema without depending on the operation contract; the leaf implementation alone binds that definition to the shared operation contract. Dependencies follow owner axes: same-operation rules, exact ancestor or cross-domain model owners, and public computation packages. Closing each admitted file to one default authority keeps strategy choice modular and transparent without hidden registries, contract cycles, whole-domain imports, operation-local policy bags, recipes, adapters, engines, private sibling operations, or unrelated implementations.
remediate: Give every implementation aggregate and leaf file one default authority and no named exports. Compose aggregate implementations only from default semantic leaf entrypoints. Keep a leaf config on authoring contracts and ancestor or public model authorities. Bind the default local operation contract and leaf strategy definition only from the leaf implementation; keep implementation dependencies on same-operation rules, ancestor model authorities, and admitted public surfaces. Promote shared policy and logic to the nearest model owner instead of creating operation-local policy or reaching into a private sibling operation.
message: Strategy dependencies must stay on the positive semantic strategy surface.
